selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What problem did the man first have with the verse about everything in the heavens and earth praising Allah?
questions.answer: He thought the verse did not seem to contain any special rhetorical power.

questions.question: What was he told to do in order to understand the verse better?
questions.answer: He was told to imagine himself going back to the time when the Qur’an was first being revealed and to hear the verse in that setting.

questions.question: How did the world appear to him before he heard the verse in that imagined scene?
questions.answer: It seemed unstable, temporary, dark, confused, empty, and lacking life, awareness, and clear purpose.

questions.question: What major change took place when he heard the verse recited?
questions.answer: The verse lifted his outlook, brightened his understanding of the universe, and made creation appear meaningful and alive with worship.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the image of the universe as a huge place of worship suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that all creation has order, meaning, and a shared role in praising Allah.

questions.question: Who is described as taking part in remembrance and glorification after the verse is heard?
questions.answer: The whole created world, especially the heavens and the earth, is described as engaged in that worship.

questions.question: How were the actions of creation described once the verse changed his view?
questions.answer: Creation was presented as joyfully and peacefully carrying out the purpose given to it.

questions.question: What did the traveler gain by comparing this verse with other verses?
questions.answer: He came to grasp one small part of the Qur’an’s deep eloquence and wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what helps explain the Qur’an’s broad historical influence?
questions.answer: Its powerful and beautiful expression helped it spread widely and maintain honor and authority for many centuries.

questions.question: Why did the listener fail at first to appreciate the verse?
questions.answer: He was judging it without entering the worldview and historical moment that would reveal its force.

questions.question: What method was used to teach him the meaning of the verse’s eloquence?
questions.answer: He was guided through an imaginative return to the period before revelation so he could feel the contrast.

questions.question: What was missing from the world as he first pictured it before hearing the verse?
questions.answer: It lacked stability, clarity, life, consciousness, and direction.

questions.question: What did the verse do to that bleak picture of existence?
questions.answer: It transformed it into a clear, illuminated, and purposeful reality.

questions.question: What does the lifting of a veil symbolize in this passage?
questions.answer: It symbolizes moving from ignorance and spiritual blindness to insight and understanding.

questions.question: How is the Qur’anic message presented in relation to later generations?
questions.answer: It is shown as instructing conscious beings across the centuries, not only people of one moment.

questions.question: What emotional tone fills creation after the verse is proclaimed?
questions.answer: The tone becomes one of gladness, contentment, and willing obedience.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach about the Qur’an’s eloquence?
questions.answer: He realized that its expressive power contains profound wisdom that can deeply reshape how reality is understood.

questions.question: What two long-term results of the Qur’an are linked to its eloquence in the passage?
questions.answer: Its spread across large parts of the world and its lasting dignity and influence over fourteen centuries.

questions.question: What verse is being reflected on in the target passage?
questions.answer: It is the verse stating that everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah.

questions.question: What was the listener’s initial judgment about that verse?
questions.answer: He thought it did not appear miraculous in its language.

questions.question: Why was he asked to picture the period before the Qur’an’s revelation?
questions.answer: So he could recognize how dramatically the verse changed the understanding of the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the condition of existence before the verse was heard?
questions.answer: It describes existence as unsettled, passing away, dark, disordered, and stripped of clear meaning.

questions.question: What effect did the recitation have on his understanding of the world?
questions.answer: It made the world seem illuminated, ordered, and full of worship and purpose.

questions.question: What does it mean that all creation was fulfilling its function?
questions.answer: It means every part of creation was seen as serving the role Allah gave it.
